title: Age-of-Information Minimization for Data Aggregation in Energy-Harvesting IoTs
problem: Energy-harvesting IoT devices struggle to maintain fresh data under energy constraints; existing AoI minimization methods ignore data aggregation scenarios.
motivation: Data freshness is critical; aggregating data from multiple sources while managing energy harvesting introduces new scheduling challenges.
method: The approach creates a two-stage transmission schedule for energy-harvesting IoT devices. First, it plans a baseline schedule offline using predictions about how much energy each device will have and when data needs to be fresh. Then it adjusts this plan in real time as actual energy conditions change, shifting which devices transmit to keep the collected data as current as possible within available power.
key_novelty: It minimizes data staleness when multiple energy-harvesting devices send sensor readings to a central collector, adapting the transmission schedule in real time to changing energy conditions.
contributions: First study of AoI minimization for data aggregation in energy-harvesting IoTs
Energy-adaptive node scheduling algorithm with offline and online components
Demonstrated high performance in AoI minimization and energy efficiency
Validated via simulation and testbed experiments
limitations: Scalability to very large-scale deployments and complex data dependencies not discussed.
primary_theme: AoI-minimizing scheduling for energy-harvesting IoT data aggregation
